beats.text: Writing a document with AI?
Today, that means copying and pasting between a chat and your draft,
a code editor where Grammarly can't follow,
or an agent that changes files you never see.
There's a better way to write.
Meet Quire.
A writing app for Typst, LaTeX, Quarto and Markdown, with your AI agent built in.
Write on one side, and see the finished page on the other.
It updates as you write. Click the page, and you jump to the line.
Need help? Ask the agent in plain words.
Draft a section, fix the grammar, or tighten your abstract.
Now, the most important part.
Nothing the agent writes lands without your say.
Every change waits for you. Accept it, reject it, or edit it first.
And if a whole turn goes wrong, undo it with one click.
To change just one sentence, select it and press Command K.
Say what you want. The agent changes only that part.
Pause while you type, and grey text suggests how the sentence goes on.
Like it? Press Tab.
Bring the AI you already pay for.
Claude, Codex, Gemini, or more than forty other agents, with your own login and your own plan.
Quire has no account of its own.
And because the editor is a real text field, Grammarly and the Mac spellchecker just work.
Everything a document needs is built in.
Cite by DOI, export to Word or PDF, find unused labels, and format in your own markup.

beats.text: Make it yours with themes.
Quire has a theme system, with several looks built in, from VS Code's dark and light to book covers and a chalkboard.
So why not just use VS Code, Cursor, or Claude Code?
They're great tools, but they're built for code.
Quire is built for documents. Previews with no setup. Grammarly that works. And every AI edit shown as a tracked change in your text.
Already use Claude Code? Keep it. Quire runs the same Claude agent, with your login.
Your files stay on your computer. No account. No telemetry.
And Quire is free and open source.
Quire. Write with AI, and keep the final say.
Download it free for Mac, Windows and Linux.
